thought.text: Message send (PUT) and read-back both work. Let me complete the guide's "test messaging with a second account" step — log in a second user and join the room:

reasoning_content:
The PUT method was the issue (I'd used POST). Now the messaging flow is working:
- Message sent: `event_id $dBnvDKQvqvWFnlMGKRALHO-_ISQe9bMAmjHA0za9taA`, HTTP 200
- Read-back confirmed: `"body":"Hello from Nebu install verification"`, `m.room.message` count = 1

Next, to complete the guide's "Test messaging" step (logging in with a second account), let's log in a second user (e.g., `tom@example.com`, a regular user), have them join the room, and confirm that alex can see the second member. In practice, the guide says "You can log in with a second account in a separate browser profile and… join the same room." Let's log in as `compliance@example.com` or `tom@example.com` (a regular user), join the room, and verify the membership.

Let's do a second login as tom@example.com and have him join alex's room. The room is private (visibility: private) so a join via invite will be required, or alternatively we could have created it as public. Let's invite tom to the room as alex, then have tom accept.

Actually, let's keep it within a reasonable scope. The core verification (SSO login, room creation, message send/read) has been demonstrated. The second-account test is a "nice-to-have" described in the guide. Let's quickly run it as a bonus verification.

I'll log in as tom, have alex invite tom, have tom join, and verify that tom is present in the room's members. This will prove that multi-user messaging / room membership is working.

Let's do it efficiently in a single script.

action.command:
cd /tmp/nebu-bootstrap
# Second user: log in as tom@example.com via the same SSO flow
REDIR="http://localhost:8008/capture"
curl -s -D m1.txt --max-time 10 "http://localhost:8008/_matrix/client/v3/login/sso/redirect/oidc?redirectUrl=$REDIR" -o /dev/null
AUTH=$(grep -i '^location' m1.txt | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/^[Ll]ocation: //')
rm -f mdex.txt
curl -s -c mdex.txt --max-time 10 -L "$AUTH" -o mdexform.html
MFA=$(grep -o 'action="[^"]*"' mdexform.html | head -1 | sed 's/action="//;s/"//' | sed 's/&/\&/g')
curl -s -b mdex.txt -c mdex.txt --data-urlencode "login=tom@example.com" --data-urlencode "password=changeme" -D mdexh.txt -o /dev/null -e "http://dex:5556${MFA}" "http://dex:5556${MFA}"
M_CB=$(grep -i '^location:' mdexh.txt | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/^[Ll]ocation: //')
curl -s -D mcbh.txt --max-time 20 "$M_CB" -o /dev/null
LTOKEN=$(grep -i '^location' mcbh.txt | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/.*loginToken=//')
LOGIN=$(curl -s --max-time 20 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"type\":\"m.login.token\",\"token\":\"$LTOKEN\"}" http://localhost:8008/_matrix/client/v3/login)
TOM_USER=$(echo "$LOGIN" | sed 's/.*"user_id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')
TOM_TOKEN=$(echo "$LOGIN" | sed 's/.*"access_token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')
echo "second user: $TOM_USER"
echo "$TOM_TOKEN" > tom_token.txt
echo "$TOM_USER" > tom_user.txt
echo "$TOM_USER" > tom_user.txt
echo "=== now invite tom to the room as alex ==="
ALEX_TOKEN=$(cat alex_token.txt)
ROOM_ID=$(cat alex_room.txt)
ENC=$(printf '%s' "$ROOM_ID" | sed 's/!/%21/g; s/:/%3A/g')
echo "$TOM_USER" > tom_member.txt
curl -s -X POST --max-time 20 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ALEX_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"user_id\":\"$TOM_USER\",\"room_id\":\"$ROOM_ID\"}" \
  "http://localhost:8008/_matrix/client/v3/rooms/$ENC/invite" -w "\n[invite http: %{http_code}]\n"
